CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
  JUNE 16, 2026 – 7:00 P.M.
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5938 KAUFFMAN AVENUE - TEMPLE CITY

PROCEDURE TO ADDRESS CITY COUNCIL:
In person: Members of the Public who wish to address the City Council may do so by completing
a Speaker Request Form, indicating the agenda item number and submitting it to the City Clerk.
Unless waived by Council, t here is a 3-minute time limit on each speaker with a maximum
period of 30 minutes for comments on any subject.

Written Comment: Written public comments received by 5pm on the day of the meeting will be
provided to the City Council and made part of the meeting record. Written public comments will
not be read aloud by city staff or City Council.
You have the opportunity to address the City Council at the following times:
  •  Agenda item: at the time the Council considers the agenda item;
  •  Non-agenda item: at the time for PUBLIC COMMENTS. Please note that while the
  City Council values your comments, pursuant to the Brown Act, the Council cannot
  take action on any item not listed on the agenda; and
  •  Public Hearing: at the time for public hearings under PUBLIC HEARING.

The listing of any item on the agenda includes the authority of the Council to take action
on such item and to approve, disapprove, or give directions on any item.

NOTICE: Staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business of this
Agenda are available for viewing on the City’s website at templecityca.gov and are on file and
available for review during regular office hours in the Office of the City Clerk located at City Hall,
9701 Las Tunas Drive, Temple City, California. Written documentation submitted to the City
Council after distribution of the agenda packet can be obtained at the City Clerk’s Office during
regular office hours.

ACCESSIBILITY: In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special
assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact the City Clerk at (626) 285-2171.
Notification 72 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements
to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

TO WATCH REGULAR MEETINGS LIVE OR RECORDED, VISIT:
https://www.youtube.com/@ConnectWithTC

AGENDA NOTIFICATION SUBSCRIPTION:
If you wish to receive an agenda email notification, please email your request to
cityclerk@templecityca.gov or call (626) 285-2171.

7. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All Consent Calendar items may be approved in a single motion as recommended

  audience wish to discuss any matters listed on the Consent Calendar, please address
  them at this time.
  Recommendation:  Approve Items A through P per recommendations.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council is requested to review and approve the:

  1. Minutes of the Special Joint Meeting of City Council and Planning Commission
  of May 28, 2026;
  2. Minutes of the City Council Budget Study Session of June 3, 2026; and
  3. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of June 3, 2026.

  Recommendation:  Approve the Minutes of the City Council Meeting.

  Attachments:  May 28, 2026 Special Joint Meeting Minutes
  June 3, 2026 Budget Study Session Minutes
  June 3, 2026 Regular Meeting Minutes

  B. PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION ACTIONS - MEETING OF May 20,
  2026

  The City Council is requested to receive and file the Parks and Recreation
  Commission Actions from their meeting on May 20, 2026.

  Recommendation:  Receive and file the Parks and Recreation
  Commission meeting actions.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  C. ADOPT  RESOLUTIONS  CONFIRMING  APPOINTMENT  OF  CITY
  COMMISSIONERS
  The City Council is requested to adopt resolutions confirming the appointment of
  city commissioners.

  Recommendations:

  1. Resolution No. 26-5884 confirming appointment of Serge Haddad and Tom
  O'Leary to the Planning Commission with term ending June 30, 2028
  (Attachment “A”);

  2. Resolution No. 26-5885 confirming appointment of Jose Tarin and Kristel
  Haddad to the Parks and Recreation Commission with term ending June 30,
  2028 (Attachment “B”);

  3. Resolution No. 26-5886 confirming appointment of Ousama Nimri and Sunny Lo
  to the Transportation and Public Safety Commission with term ending June 30,
  2028 (Attachment “C”); and

  4. Direct the City Clerk to arrange for all appointees to receive their official Oath of
  Office at the next Council meeting.
  Attachment:  Staff Report

  D. SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 26-1088, AMENDING
  CHAPTERS 9-2 (SUBDIVISION REGULATIONS) AND 9-3 (CONDOMINIUM
  CONVERSIONS), AND DELETING CHAPTERS 9-4 (CONDOMINIUM
  CONSTRUCTIONS) AND 9-6 (VESTING TENTATIVE MAPS) OF THE TEMPLE
  CITY MUNICIPAL CODE
  The City Council is requested to adopt an ordinance amending various sections of
  the Temple City Municipal Code (TCMC) related to subdivision and condominium
  conversion regulations.

June 16, 2026

  Recommendation:  Adopt Ordinance No. 26-1088 amending
  Chapters 9-2 (Subdivision Regulations) And 9-3
  (Condominium Conversions), and deleting
  Chapters 9-4 (Condominium Constructions) and
  9-6 (Vesting Tentative Maps) of the Temple City
  Municipal Code.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  E. APPROVAL OF AGREEMENT WITH THE INLAND VALLEY HUMANE SOCIETY &
  S.P.C.A. FOR ANIMAL CONTROL, SHELTERING, AND PET LICENSING
  SERVICES
  The City Council is requested to approve an agreement for animal control,
  sheltering, and pet license services.

  Recommendation:

  1. Approve a new agreement between the City of Temple City and the Inland
  Valley Humane Society & S.P.C.A. (IVHS) for animal control, sheltering, and pet
  licensing services for Fiscal Years (FY) 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 (Attachment
  “A”); and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  F. APPROVAL OF A CONSULTANT SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH LEAD TECH
  ENVIRONMENTAL TO PROVIDE ASBESTOS AND LEAD-BASED PAINT
  TESTING SERVICES FOR THE CITY’S HOME IMPROVEMENT PROGRAMS

  The City council is requested to approve a consultant services agreement to
  provide asbestos and lead-based paint testing services for the City's Home
  Improvement Programs.

  Recommendation:

  1. Review and approve a consultant services agreement (Attachment “A”) with
  Lead Tech Environmental (Lead Tech) to provide asbestos, lead, and mold
  consulting services for an initial three-year term, with one optional one-year
  extension, for a total compensation not to exceed $45,000 during the initial term;

  2. Authorize the City Manager to finalize and execute the consultant services
  agreement for three years beginning on July 1, 2026; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to exercise the optional one-year extension if
  compensation for the extension year does not exceed $15,000.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  G. PURCHASE AND INSTALLATION OF BLADE SIGNS FOR THE LAS TUNAS
  DRIVE STREETSCAPE PROJECT

  The City Council is requested to authorize the City manager to execute a contract
  for the purchase and installation of blade signs for participating businesses in the
  Las Tunas Drive Streetscape Project.

  Recommendation:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute a contract and/or purchase order with
  ASI Sign Systems, Inc. (ASI), through the State of California Multiple Award
  Schedules (CMAS) Program, for the purchase and installation of blade signs for
  participating businesses in the Las Tunas Drive Streetscape Project, in an
  amount not to exceed $33,912.05, which includes a 10 percent contingency for
  unforeseen issues;

  2. Authorize the City Manager to approve related non-substantive changes and
  execute any documents necessary to implement the purchase and installation;
  and

  3. Waive fees related to building plan check, building permit, and encroachment
  permits.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  H. FIRST AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT WITH ULTIMATE MAINTENANCE
  SERVICE, INC. FOR CITYWIDE JANITORIAL SERVICES

  The City Council is requested to authorize the City Manager to execute a first
  amendment to the agreement with Ultimate Maintenance Services, Inc. extending
  the term of the agreement by three months (July 1, 2026 to September 30, 2026) in
  order to conduct a Request for Proposals for janitorial services.

  Recommendation:  Authorize the City Manager to execute a first
  amendment to the agreement with Ultimate
  Maintenance Services, Inc., extending the term of
  agreement by three months, for citywide janitorial
  services.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

June 16, 2026

  I. APPROVE THE AGREEMENT FOR INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SUPPORT
  SERVICES WITH THE CITY OF BREA/BREAIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-2027

  support services for Fiscal Year 2026-2027.

  Recommendation:

  1. Approve the Agreement for Services with the City of Brea/BreaIT for information
  technology support for the period of July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Agreement.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  J. APPROVAL OF SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE AGREEMENT  WITH
  CLIFTONLARSONALLEN, LLP FOR PROFESSIONAL AUDIT SERVICES
  The City Council is requested to approve a second amendment to the agreement
  for professional audit services.

  Recommendation:
  1. Approve a Second Amendment to the agreement with CliftonLarsonAllen, LLP
  (Attachment "A") for a final one-year term extension for professional audit
  services; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to sign and execute the Agreement.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  K. APPROVAL OF A SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH GERALD A. JAMBAZIAN FOR
  PHOTOGRAPHY SERVICES AND TEMPLECITYPHOTOS.COM WEBSITE
  MAINTENANCE

  The City Council is requested to approve a services agreement for photography
  services and its website maintenance.

  Recommendation:

  1. Approve a one-year Services Agreement with Gerald A. Jambazian (Attachment
  “A”) in an amount not to exceed $17,500, covering the period of July 5, 2026,
  through July 5, 2027, for professional photography services and maintenance of
  the TempleCityPhotos.com website; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Services Agreement.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  L. APPROVAL OF ANNUAL PROFESSIONAL SERVICE AGREEMENT WITH THE
  TEMPLE CITY CHAMBER OF COMMERCE

  The City Council is requested to approve an annual professional service agreement

  Recommendation:

  1. Approve a Professional Services Agreement with the Temple City Chamber of
  Commerce for business promotion and public information services (Attachment

  2027; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to sign and execute the agreement.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  M. FINAL SUBDIVISION MAP APPROVAL FOR PARCEL MAP NO. 84038, A three-
  unit condominium SUBDIVISION AT 5935 Kauffman Avenue

  The City Council is requested to approve the final map which will allow the property
  owner to record the subdivision.

  Recommendation:

  1. Review and approve the final subdivision map for Parcel Map No. 84038
  (Attachment “A”); and

  2. Authorize the City Clerk to certify Parcel Map No. 84038.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  N. SECOND AMENDMENT TO LEGAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH BURKE,
  WILLIAMS & SORENSEN, LLP
  The City Council is requested to approve the second amendment to the city's legal
  services agreement.

  Recommendation:

  1. Approve a Second Amendment to Legal Services Agreement between the
  City and Burke, Williams & Sorenson, LLP (“Burke”), modernizing the rate
  structure, eliminating the tiered partner rate schedule, and establishing an
  automatic annual Consumer Price Index (CPI-U) adjustment mechanism

  effective July 1, 2026; and

  2.  Authorize the City Manager to execute the Second Amendment to the
  Service Agreement.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  O. THIRD AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT FOR SERVICES WITH DAPEER,
  ROSENBILT & LITVAK, LLP

  The City Council is requested to approve a third amendment to the service
  agreement for code enforcement attorneys.

  Recommendation:

  1. Approve a Third Amendment to Agreement for Services between the City and
  Dapeer, Rosenbilt & Litvak, LLP , updating the rate structure into a single hourly
  rate of $295.00, introducing a rate provision for matters outside of regular code
  enforcement, and establishing an automatic annual Consumer Price Index (CPI)
  adjustment mechanism not to exceed 3% per year, effective July 1, 2026.

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Third Amendment to the Agreement
  for Services.

  Attachment:  Staff Report

  The City Council is requested to adopt Resolution No. 26-5880 authorizing the
